intended: All four blocks sit on one farm in one summer, and a single rainfall record covers every case at once. The mid-passage facts state that rainfall in each block's season ran about a fifth above the year before and that every block lay in open ground, under no cover, and the extra water fell on every block whose yield was measured. Each block is compared against itself a season earlier rather than against an undripped block in the same season, and the rain and the drip line moved together. The 0.4 to 0.7 tonne gains cannot be separated from the wetter season. The population and completeness clauses in the same line describe a tally with no gap between the ground measured and the ground the claim covers, so the rainfall is the whole of the defect.
reported: A named alternative cause reaches every block: "Rainfall in each block's season ran about a fifth above the year before, and every block lay in open ground, under no cover." A 20 percent wetter season on uncovered maize would raise yield by itself, so the 0.4-0.7 t/ha gains are not attributable to the drip line.

intended: In cases one and three the comprehension score was recorded before the program began: 11 September precedes 6 December at Ashcombe Primary, and 24 April precedes 20 June at Halloway Junior. Half the evidence therefore describes gains that were already in place when the classes started the program, so it cannot be evidence for the program. The two remaining cases, Deerpark Academy and Marchfield Grange, are too few to establish the claim on their own.

reported: Two of the four classes are scored before the program began: Ashcombe 'started the program 6 December' but scored higher 'by 11 September than the previous autumn term' (11 Sep precedes 6 Dec inside the autumn term), and Halloway 'started the program 20 June' but scored higher 'by 24 April than the previous spring term' (24 Apr precedes 20 Jun inside the spring term). The other two classes (8 Jan to 12 Mar, 6 Jul to 21 Aug) run forward within their named term.

intended: All four sections sit at Harlow in one autumn term, and a single change to the central syllabus covers every case at once. The mid-passage facts state that the central syllabus set coursework at a third of the final grade, up from a quarter, and that every section was marked to that central syllabus, putting the heavier share over every section whose completion was measured. Each section is compared against itself a year earlier under the smaller share, leaving the kit and the larger share moving together across the 6 to 11 point rises. The population and completeness clauses in the same line describe a tally with no gap between the students counted and the students the claim covers, leaving the syllabus change the whole of the defect.
reported: A named alternative cause reaches all four sections: 'The central syllabus set coursework at a third of the final grade, up from a quarter, and every section was marked to that central syllabus.' Raising coursework's weight from 25 to 33 percent of the final grade would by itself raise coursework completion, so the 6-to-11-point gains cannot be attributed to the lab kit.

intended: The mid-passage line tallies the averages over the patients who kept up the home exercises, and the clause beside it records that a quarter of each intake let those exercises lapse. The claim is about the protocol restoring shoulder range of motion for the patients put on it, so the population is the whole intake and the averages describe three quarters of it. Patients whose shoulders stay stiff and painful are the ones who let the exercises go, so the quarter held out of the average is where the flat and negative results sit and the reported figures are an average over the patients who were already doing well. The four intakes span four hospitals, four injury types, four seasons and four therapists, and the lapsed quarter applies to each intake, so the same quarter is absent from every case rather than being covered by any of them.
reported: 'Averages cover the patients who kept up the home exercises, and a quarter of each intake let the home exercises lapse' - the 9-16 degree gains are measured only on the compliant three-quarters, excluding the lapsed quarter, so the numbers describe a self-selected subgroup rather than the intakes that completed the protocol.

intended: All four plots are tomatoes in the Ellis backyard in one summer, and a single rainfall record covers every case at once. The mid-passage facts state that rainfall in each plot's season ran a fifth higher than the year before and that every plot stood in the open, on no set watering schedule, and the extra water fell on every plot whose plants were measured. Each plot is compared against itself a season earlier rather than against an unfertilised plot in the same season, and the rain and the feeding moved together. The 8 to 13 centimetre gains cannot be separated from the wetter season. The population and completeness clauses in the same line describe a tally with no gap between the plants measured and the plants the claim covers.
reported: Rainfall in each plot's season 'ran a fifth higher than the year before' and 'every plot stood in the open, on no set watering schedule', so the extra water actually reached every plant and was not offset by controlled irrigation; a 20 percent rainfall increase is an alternative cause of the 8-13 cm height gains that fits all four plots.
